title: Release-lock behavior and semantic mapping for model version selectors
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem:

Teams onboarding new models need deterministic, debuggable semantics when clients specify a model using one of: a commit hash (e.g. sha256), a semantic version (semver, possibly range), or an arbitrary tag/alias (e.g. 'stable', 'dev', 'redwood-optimized'). Today SDKs and the runtime sometimes differ in how they resolve these selectors, which causes surprises: silent fallbacks to older binaries, cache thrashing, or unexpected perf regressions.

Goal:

Define a single, forward-compatible mapping of selector types to resolution behavior for both the SDK (client-side validation + optional pre-resolution) and the Control Plane/Runtime (authoritative resolution). The contract must be: deterministic, observable (audit events), safe (no silent degrading of guarantees without explicit opt-in), and incremental (migration path for existing pinned references).

Proposal summary (high level):

- Selector precedence (strict): exact-commit-hash > exact-semver (==1.2.3) > semver-range (>=1.2 <2.0) > tag/alias > implicit-latest.
- No silent downward fallback: when a selector resolves to a model that is incompatible with the requested "profile" (performance or API surface), resolution must either return an informative error with suggested fallback targets or follow an explicit fallback policy attached to the request.
- Tags are mutable labels that map to a concrete model reference. Tag-to-ref changes must be recorded; tag-unwrap (resolve-to-commit) is authoritative in Control Plane and emits an audit record.
- Semver handling: semver ranges resolve to the highest matching stable release unless a policy flag `include-prerelease` is present. We treat build metadata and pre-release labels conservatively by default.
- SDK behavior: by default SDKs will send the raw selector to the Control Plane for authoritative resolution. Optionally, the SDK can perform a local sanity-check (validate semver grammar, detect obviously malformed hashes) and, when configured with `pre-resolve:true`, expand tags/ranges to an exact internal ref and include that resolved-ref in the request for caching/stabilization purposes.
- Runtime caching: cache keys are based on resolved concrete model refs, not the original selector. When clients include both selector and resolved-ref, Control Plane will validate consistency and prefer the explicit resolved-ref for routing.
notes: 2025-02-15: Initial draft circulated to runtime and sdk teams. Collected early feedback about semver range edge cases and compatibility with existing cache invalidation logic.
2025-02-18: Design sync with infra: confirmed ability to emit tag-change audit events and maintain short-term rollback history for tags for 72 hours.
2025-02-21: Runtime team reported that kernel-level incompatibilities (quantization variant) must be surfaced as a compatibility constraint; added a compatibility label to resolution outputs.
2025-02-28: Security requested explicit flag for `allow-unverified-fallbacks` to prevent automatic fallbacks in high-compliance customers. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-03: SDK PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/824 introduces optional `pre_resolve` and local semver validation. Waiting on runtime API review for `resolved_ref` field schema.
acceptance_criteria: Control Plane exposes a deterministic resolution endpoint that accepts selector types {commit, semver, semver-range, tag} and returns a concrete model_ref plus compatibility metadata.
SDK default behavior: forward selector to Control Plane; optional `pre_resolve` expands to concrete ref and sends both selector and resolved_ref.
No silent fallback: if a compatible model cannot be selected, runtime returns 409 with structured diagnostics and suggested fallbacks unless `allow-unverified-fallbacks=true` is explicitly set.
All tag updates write audit entries and retain the previous mapping for 72 hours for debugging/rollback.
Unit + integration tests covering semver edge cases, pre-release handling, and migration scenarios.
testing_plan: Unit tests: semver parser, range resolution, pre-release flags.
Integration: SDK->ControlPlane resolution with/without pre_resolve, verifying cache keys are concrete refs.
Canary rollout: enable `pre_resolve` in non-prod SDK builds to detect mismatch rates between client-resolved refs and server resolution; threshold alarms if mismatch > 0.1%.
Chaos test: simulate tag flip during in-flight requests and assert audit events + request determinism (either use original resolved ref or fail with diagnostic).
implementation_notes: Control Plane: add /resolve endpoint and store mapping history at tag namespace level.
Runtime: ensure cache key generation uses concrete model_ref; accept optional `resolved_ref` header for strict routing path.
SDK: add semver validation utilities and `pre_resolve` opt-in. Deprecate any client-side heuristics that guess latest matching semver without server confirmation.
Telemetry: emit resolution.method=(server|sdk_pre_resolve), resolution.selector_type, resolved_ref, compatibility.flags, tag_change events.
